figure_inventory.description: Checked against the page picture (24 spokes, one straight up). Illustrates the wheel the text already describes: The Ashoka Chakra drawn in navy blue on white: an outer circular rim with small scalloped bumps along its inner edge, a solid round hub at the centre, and 24 slender spokes (thin and tapering) from the hub to the rim, equally spaced 15 degrees apart (one spoke straight up, one horizontal). Spoke count 24 verified by sampling a circle round the hub.

Checked against the page picture. Coloured architectural illustration of the building, not redrawable faithfully; the question is about its outer boundary, drawn from P23-shape-2. A coloured flat-style illustration (left of the outline) of the new Parliament Building in Delhi seen from the front-above: a three-sided (triangular, corners cut off) building. The front face is in the middle bottom with a central entrance (brown door with steps, two tall windows with vertical dark bars on each side of the door); the two side faces slant away to the left and right with rows of tall narrow windows. Inside the courtyard on top there is a central tower/dome with a small emblem on top and three green trees at the front. Colours are shades of terracotta, pink, brown and cream.

Checked against the page picture (side ratio measured about 3.8:1). A single closed outline in thin brown-pink colour (no fill, no dot, no labels): a hexagon with all interior angles 120 degrees and sides alternately long and short. From the top, clockwise: a long horizontal top side, a short side sloping down to the right, a long side sloping down to the left (lower-right edge), a short horizontal bottom side, a long side sloping up to the left (lower-left edge), and a short side sloping up to the right back to the start of the top side (upper-left corner cut). In other words it is an equilateral triangle pointing DOWNWARD with its three corners cut off. Long side to short side ratio is about 3.8 to 1.

Checked against the page picture. The tile design is drawn in every cell of that item's grid figure. A small square tile split by a diagonal from the bottom-left corner to the top-right corner into two right triangles: the upper-left triangle is blue and the lower-right triangle is yellow. No outline other than the colour edge.

Checked against the page picture and re-read by pixel sampling of all 16 tiles: matches. A square grid of 8 columns by 8 rows of equal squares (thin black lines). Two thick red lines cross at the middle of the grid: a vertical red line between column 4 and column 5 from the top edge to the bottom edge, and a horizontal red line between row 4 and row 5 from the left edge to the right edge; they cut the grid into four 4 x 4 quarters. Only the TOP-LEFT quarter (columns 1-4, rows 1-4, 16 squares) is filled; the other three quarters (48 squares) are empty white. Every one of the 16 filled squares is a colour tile: a square cut along one diagonal into a blue triangle and a yellow triangle. Notation: '/' = diagonal from bottom-left corner to top-right corner, UL = upper-left triangle, LR = lower-right triangle; '\' = diagonal from top-left corner to bottom-right corner, UR = upper-right triangle, LL = lower-left triangle. Rows from the top, columns from the left: Row 1: c1 '/' UL blue, LR yellow; c2 '/' UL yellow, LR blue; c3 '/' UL blue, LR yellow; c4 '/' UL yellow, LR blue. Row 2: c1 '/' UL yellow, LR blue; c2 '/' UL blue, LR yellow; c3 '/' UL yellow, LR blue; c4 '\' UR blue, LL yellow. Row 3: c1 '/' UL blue, LR yellow; c2 '/' UL yellow, LR blue; c3 '/' UL yellow, LR blue; c4 '\' UR yellow, LL blue. Row 4: c1 '/' UL yellow, LR blue; c2 '\' UR yellow, LL blue; c3 '\' UR blue, LL yellow; c4 '/' UL blue, LR yellow. Blue is a medium cornflower blue, yellow a soft golden yellow. The two red lines are presumably the two lines of symmetry the completed design must have.

Checked against the page picture. The rules are fully stated in the text; the figure only shows two example moves. A 6 by 6 grid of equal squares (thin black lines, 36 squares, no numbers). Two example lines are already drawn, each a short black line segment with a black dot at each end, joining the centres of two adjacent squares: (1) horizontal, in the top row (row 1), joining the centres of the squares in column 3 and column 4; (2) vertical, in column 2, joining the centres of the squares in row 2 and row 3. The two lines do not touch or overlap.

Checked against the page picture. Illustrates the rule 'the lines cannot overlap' already stated in the text. A small 2 by 2 grid of squares (thin black lines) with the red label 'Not allowed' above it (red text) and a red cross mark (an X) above its right-hand square. Two lines with dots at both ends are drawn on it: a horizontal line across the TOP row joining the centres of the two top squares (dots at the middles of top-left and top-right squares), and a vertical line in the RIGHT column joining the top-right square and the bottom-right square (its upper dot sits just below the right dot of the horizontal line, inside the top-right square; its lower dot is in the bottom-right square). So both lines cover the top-right square, which is the overlap that is not allowed.

Checked against the page picture. A plus/cross made of two overlapping rectangles (a tall vertical one about 4.3 times as tall as wide and a wide horizontal one of the same size crossing in the middle; the centre square is outlined with all 4 sides), black outline. FOUR dashed lines through the centre, each extending beyond the figure: vertical, horizontal and two diagonals at 45 degrees (a small X of dashes is visible in the centre square). To its left: 'Numbers of line symmetry = 4' and 'Order of rotational symmetry = 4'.

Checked against the page picture. A flower of four lens-shaped petals (each pointed at both ends) meeting at a centre point, the petals pointing diagonally (up-left, up-right, down-left, down-right); black outline. Checked against the page picture. Part c: a parallelogram (not a rhombus, not a rectangle), black outline, no dashed lines: horizontal top and bottom edges of equal length (about 158 units) with the top edge shifted to the right of the bottom edge by about 51 units (the slanted sides lean to the right, length about 142), height about 133. The label 'c.' is printed below-left of it. Text at the right below: 'No line of symmetry' and '2 angles (180 degrees, 360 degrees)'.
